what_it_does: MetoHash is a data structure for fast key-value lookups that spans three levels of storage to balance speed and cost. It uses CPU caches for initial inserts, DRAM (fast, volatile memory) for intermediate organization, and PMem (persistent memory that survives power loss) for long-term storage. The system batches updates before moving data down the hierarchy to reduce unnecessary writes. It also uses fingerprinting to avoid checking persistent memory when not needed.
